label: receipts
tail:
Both receipts are complete and the gate is green — **0 errors, 96 warnings, exit 0**, run twice, the second time against the exact bytes delivered.

**Spine receipt** (`research/frontier-17-spine-audit.json`) was stale, but not for a mathematical reason. Against a freshly generated template the 58 ids, their rank order, every `direct_consumers` count and every `content_sha256` are identical to the 6c reading; `transitive_consumers` moved by a **uniform +3** on all 58 and none of the 58 is inside this run's `item_scope`. The +3 is exactly the three items step 9 built (`ex-orthogonal-group-is-a-regular-level-set`, `ex-lagrange-multipliers-with-two-constraints`, `cor-index-of-a-full-rank-integer-sublattice-is-the-absolute-determinant`) appearing downstream of the whole foundational spine. I refreshed the scope block and `scope_sha256`, kept all 58 attestations, and recorded the checks in `reviewer`. Those attestations are carried readings validated by hash, not fresh reads — nothing had changed to re-read.

**Audit receipt** (`research/frontier-17-audit-coverage.json`): reviewer, attestation, and **78 plan-reconciliation rows with 78 concrete reasons, 0 blank**. For each I opened the item, located the fact label or `Given` clause carrying each added dependency and the step citing it, and confirmed each dropped dependency has no `[[id]]` link in the body. I then re-checked every reason that asserted scaffold intent against that row's own `planned_deps` and corrected ten — most substantively `thm-no-retraction-of-the-closed-disk-onto-the-circle`, where the scaffold *had* planned the trivial-fundamental-group theorem and the real drift is the norm inequality verifying its convexity hypothesis. One dropped dependency is deliberate and flagged: `ex-sine-of-xy-and-its-mixed-partials` says in its Remark that it computes the mixed partials directly, so it is an instance of Clairaut rather than an application.

The drift is mostly one shape — the scaffold planned the big theorem and not the fact that checks its hypothesis — plus a handful of genuine route changes, four Statements that now declare countable choice out loud, and three definitions discharging their own well-definedness.

Nothing about the mathematics is being papered over: `judge-closure.json` independently reports scope 443, all pairs complete, 0 needing rejudge, 0 unadjudicated, 0 open fatal, and `defect-ledger check` is clean at 333 rows. All 96 warnings are the single class `judge-verdict-adjudicated-nonfatal` across 89 items — 92 `confirmed_nonfatal`, 4 `false_positive`, none fatal.

One thing worth carrying to step 10: of those 96 current rejections, **88 are DeepSeek and 8 are Opus**. The cross-family lane is doing eleven times the screening work, which is the expected shape under `deepseek+opus` and not an anomaly. Three of the four `false_positive` calls are DeepSeek; the fourth, `fs-one-existing-iterated-integral-guarantees-multiple-riemann-integrability`, is an Opus rejection dismissed by an Anthropic-family Alpha — named in the report so step 10 weighs it rather than counts it.

Report at `research/frontier-17-alpha-receipts.md`.
